This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and efficacy of recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase (rhG

papers.title: Extension Study of Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Myozyme in Patients With Pompe Disease Who Were Previously Enrolled in Genzyme Sponsored Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) Studies
papers.summary: This extension study was to monitor the long-term safety and efficacy of rhGAA treatment in patients with infantile-onset Pompe disease who were previously treated with rhGAA derived from the Synpac cell line

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of AB-1009 Gene Therapy (GAA Gene) in Adult Participants With Late-Onset Pompe Disease (PROGRESS-GT LOPD)
papers.summary: This is a single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety, tolerability and efficacy of a single intravenous infusion of AB-1009 in adult participants with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD).

papers.title: A Gene Transfer Study for Late-Onset Pompe Disease (RESOLUTE)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of a single intravenous infusion of SPK-3006 in adults with clinically moderate, late-onset Pompe disease receiving enzyme replacement therapy (ERT). Participants will be treated in sequential, dose-level cohorts.

papers.title: Immune Modulation Therapy for Pompe Disease
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess anti-recombinant human acid α-glucosidase (anti-rhGAA) antibody titers after treatment with immune modulation therapy in patients of Pompe disease.

papers.title: Rescue of neurologic disease in mucopolysaccharidosis type II mice via AAV-mediated liver delivery of brain-penetrating iduronate-2-sulfatase.
papers.summary: In MPS II knockout mice, liver-directed AAV8.LSP.IVS2.eBT-IDS4 restored substantial brain iduronate-2-sulfatase activity, normalized glycosaminoglycan accumulation and neuropathology, and improved cognitive, skeletal, and cardiac abnormalities. The transferable strategy is systemic hepatic delivery of a brain-penetrant lysosomal enzyme, but this paper does not test or mention the input Pompe disease mechanism, acid α-glucosidase deficiency.

papers.title: Liver Gene Therapy in Fabry Disease Mice With Low Doses of rAAV2/8 Expressing a Codon-Optimized hGLA cDNA Results in Long-Term Disease Correction.
papers.summary: In juvenile Gla-knockout mice, intravenous liver-directed AAV8-pSMD2_hGLA_CO2 produced sustained circulating α-Gal A, normalized lyso-Gb3 in plasma and major tissues, and restored thermal nociception for more than 11 months. The study supports liver-directed enzyme replacement as a transferable strategy for restoring a deficient lysosomal hydrolase, although the intervention targets GLA/α-Gal A rather than acid α-glucosidase.

papers.title: Lipid Nanoparticle-Delivered mRNA Therapy Corrects Neonatal Murine MPS I-H.
papers.summary: The paper shows that lipid nanoparticle-delivered mRNA encoding human IDUA fused to a melanotransferrin peptide increased IDUA activity and reduced biochemical and neurodevelopmental disease features in neonatal MPS I-H mice. The treatment provided evidence for hepatic delivery and partial central nervous system penetration, although the experiment was conducted in mice rather than patients with Pompe Disease or with an acid α-glucosidase-deficiency model.

papers.title: Encapsulated cells as an enzyme replacement therapy for metachromatic leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: In mice with established metachromatic leukodystrophy, an implanted cell-based device continuously delivered recombinant human arylsulfatase A, was well tolerated for three months, corrected sulfatide storage, and improved central nervous system neuroinflammation. The study supports encapsulated-cell enzyme delivery as a potential therapy for symptomatic MLD, but it does not test acid α-glucosidase deficiency or Pompe disease.

papers.title: Progress and Challenges in the Treatment of Fabry Disease.
papers.summary: This review describes interventions for Fabry disease that restore or increase lysosomal α-galactosidase A activity, including recombinant-enzyme replacement, pharmacological chaperoning, gene transfer, messenger RNA delivery, and enzyme-containing vesicles or nanoparticles. It also identifies delivery and immunogenicity limitations relevant to optimizing enzyme replacement for other lysosomal disorders, including Pompe disease.

papers.title: Cardiac manifestations of Fabry disease.
papers.summary: This review shows that Fabry disease, a lysosomal enzyme deficiency caused by pathogenic GLA variants, is clinically managed with enzyme replacement therapy and α-galactosidase A pharmacological chaperones that can improve cardiac measures and slow disease progression. Its delivery limitations, incomplete tissue distribution, persistence of fibrosis despite clearance of Gb3, and development of substrate-reduction and gene therapies identify optimization strategies and warning signs that may inform approaches to treating lysosomal hydrolase deficiencies such as acid α-glucosidase deficiency in Pompe disease.

papers.title: Pompe's disease.
papers.summary: This review describes Pompe disease as an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency and lysosomal glycogen storage, with cardiac hypertrophy as a key feature of classic infantile disease. It identifies enzyme replacement therapy using recombinant human alpha-glucosidase, alglucosidase alfa, as an approved treatment that changed disease prospects and transformed care.

papers.title: A randomized study of alglucosidase alfa in late-onset Pompe's disease.
papers.summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled trial found that biweekly intravenous alglucosidase alfa improved walking distance and stabilized pulmonary function in ambulatory patients with late-onset Pompe's disease over 78 weeks. The paper identifies Pompe's disease as a deficiency of acid alpha glucosidase, an enzyme that degrades lysosomal glycogen, while also reporting infusion-related adverse reactions.

papers.title: Human acid alpha-glucosidase from rabbit milk has therapeutic effect in mice with glycogen storage disease type II.
papers.summary: Recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase produced in transgenic rabbit milk corrected enzyme deficiency throughout all tested tissues except brain after one intravenous dose in a knockout mouse model of glycogen storage disease type II. Weekly infusions for six months degraded lysosomal glycogen in heart, skeletal muscle, and smooth muscle and substantially improved tissue morphology.

papers.title: Morphological changes in muscle tissue of patients with infantile Pompe's disease receiving enzyme replacement therapy.
papers.summary: In four children with classic infantile Pompe's disease, 72 weeks of intravenous recombinant human alpha-glucosidase reduced lysosomal glycogen storage and substantially improved muscle architecture in the least affected patient. Responses varied among patients, and the authors concluded that benefit depends partly on baseline glycogen burden and muscle pathology and on treatment before irreversible damage.

papers.title: Receptor-mediated uptake of acid alpha-glucosidase corrects lysosomal glycogen storage in cultured skeletal muscle.
papers.summary: In cultured skeletal muscle cells from an infant with Pompe disease, a mannose-6-phosphate receptor-targeted acid alpha-glucosidase precursor was internalized, delivered to lysosomes, and converted into mature enzyme. The treatment reversed accumulated glycogen storage, providing in vitro evidence for receptor-mediated enzyme replacement.

papers.title: Multiple muscles in the AMD quail can be "cross-corrected" of pathologic glycogen accumulation after intravenous injection of an [E1-, polymerase-] adenovirus vector encoding human acid-alpha-glucosidase.
papers.summary: Intravenous delivery of an [E1-, E2b-] adenovirus vector encoding human acid alpha-glucosidase produced liver transduction, hepatic secretion and uptake of the enzyme by cardiac and skeletal muscle lysosomes in a quail model of acid maltase deficiency. The delivered enzyme was proteolytically processed and cleared pathologic glycogen accumulation in multiple AMD muscles, supporting liver-directed hGAA gene transfer as a cross-correction strategy.

papers.title: Aminoguanidine hemisulfate improves mitochondrial autophagy, oxidative stress, and muscle force in Duchenne muscular dystrophy via the AKT/FOXO1 pathway in mdx mice.
papers.summary: In young male mdx mice modeling Duchenne muscular dystrophy, aminoguanidine hemisulfate restored abnormal autophagy markers, increased Pink1 and Parkin expression, and reversed reduced mitochondrial DNA content. The treatment also reduced oxidative stress and apoptosis, improved muscle histology and force, and was linked experimentally to modulation of the AKT/FOXO1 pathway; transfer to Pompe disease remains untested.

papers.title: Leucyl-tRNA Synthetase Contributes to Muscle Weakness through Mammalian Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 Activation and Autophagy Suppression in a Mouse Model of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: In the dystrophin-deficient mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, elevated LeuRS activates RagD–mTORC1 signaling, increases ULK1 phosphorylation, suppresses autophagy, and contributes to muscle weakness. The small-molecule LeuRS–RagD interaction inhibitor BC-LI-0186 reduced mTORC1 signaling, restored autophagy, reduced muscle damage, and partially rescued muscle strength; chloroquine blockade abolished the force benefit, supporting an autophagy-dependent effect.

papers.title: Autophagy activation via BAG3 gene therapy improves phenotype in a mouse model of LGMD1A.
papers.summary: Systemic AAVrh74.tMCK.hBAG3 gene therapy reduced myotilin aggregate burden, prevented autophagy overload, and improved motor and muscle-function outcomes in the TgT57I mouse model of LGMD1A. Molecular assays showed normalization of p62 and LC3-II/LC3-I levels, while the endogenous BAG1/BAG3 ratio returned to a level comparable with younger untreated mice.

papers.title: Metformin restores autophagic flux and mitochondrial function in late passage myoblast to impede age-related muscle loss.
papers.summary: In a late-passage C2C12 myoblast model of age-related muscle loss, metformin reduced cellular-senescence markers, restored myogenic differentiation, and improved autophagic flux and mitochondrial function. The study proposes that enhanced autophagic activity contributes to these beneficial effects and supports metformin as a potential treatment for sarcopenia.

papers.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acids prevent myosteatosis and lipotoxicity.
papers.summary: In palmitic acid-induced C2C12 myotube myosteatosis, lipid accumulation, ceramide and diacylglycerol increases, impaired insulin-stimulated protein synthesis, and reduced autophagic flux preceded cell death. Co-incubation with DHA or ARA prevented the palmitic acid-associated cell death, while DHA and ARA completely reversed the protein-synthesis defect and partially reduced ceramide and diacylglycerol accumulation.

papers.title: Running improves muscle mass by activating autophagic flux and inhibiting ubiquitination degradation in mdx mice.
papers.summary: In mdx mice, 10 weeks of treadmill training improved muscle mass, strength, endurance, fatigue resistance, and regeneration while reducing muscle-protein ubiquitination and degradation. Running also increased the suppressed autophagic flux, supporting exercise as an intervention on a mechanism relevant to accumulated lysosomal-material clearance and muscle dysfunction.

papers.title: The remarkable effects of the ionized medical water Asea<sup>®</sup> in 3 boys with Duchenne dystrophy: Three case reports.
papers.summary: In a three-case, uncontrolled series of boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Asea® redox supplement—usually combined with L-carnitine and omega-3 fatty acids—was associated with lower rhabdomyolysis biomarkers and some functional improvements. The paper attributes the effect to NRF2 activation, increased endogenous antioxidant enzyme activity, and reduced oxidative stress, but in vivo antioxidant markers were not measured and the findings require controlled validation.

papers.title: Muscle strength, quantity and quality and muscle fat quantity and their association with oxidative stress in patients with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy: Effect of antioxidant supplementation.
papers.summary: In a study of 32 adults with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), quadriceps weakness and reduced muscle quality were associated with increased oxidative stress. In 20 FSHD patients receiving antioxidant supplementation or placebo, supplementation altered non-dominant quadriceps muscle and fat volumes and dominant quadriceps muscle quality, and was associated with improved quadriceps strength and antioxidant response.

papers.title: Cilostazol attenuates oxidative stress and apoptosis in the quadriceps muscle of the dystrophic mouse experimental model.
papers.summary: In quadriceps muscle from 14-day-old mdx mice, 14 days of cilostazol reduced reactive oxygen species production, lipofuscin granules, lipid peroxidation, and apoptotic cells, indicating antioxidant and anti-apoptotic effects in a dystrophic muscle model. The study provides an intervention and outcome measures for assessing oxidative stress and apoptosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Deletion of Dux ameliorates muscular dystrophy in mdx mice by attenuating oxidative stress via Nrf2.
papers.summary: In mdx mice, deletion of Dux improved skeletal-muscle strength and contractility, reduced fibrosis, inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, and promoted muscle satellite-cell proliferation and survival. The paper attributes these benefits to increased Nrf2 levels, making Dux deletion an intervention that attenuates oxidative stress in a dystrophy model.

papers.title: DP71 supports early homeostatic adaptation in DP427-deficient muscle cells
papers.summary: The paper shows that retention of the short dystrophin isoform DP71 creates an early adaptive state in DP427-deficient human myotubes, characterized by reduced reactive oxygen species production, lower intracellular calcium, improved viability, and preservation of membrane–cytoskeletal homeostasis. Complete loss of dystrophin isoforms produces stronger structural and stress-associated abnormalities, while DP71 does not restore full structural maturation.

papers.title: Iron supplementation alleviates pathologies in a mouse model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In a DUX4-expressing mouse model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), iron supplementation and ferrostatin-1 improved physical function and suppressed lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial superoxide, oxidative DNA damage, and ferroptosis-related signaling. Iron chelation, an iron-deficient diet, and Irp2 deficiency did not improve and generally worsened disease outcomes, showing that the relationship between iron availability and oxidative injury is disease-model dependent.

papers.title: Immune tolerance induction for laronidase treatment in mucopolysaccharidosis I.
papers.summary: A small, prematurely terminated Phase 2 trial found no successful immune tolerance induction in 3/3 severe MPS I patients receiving prophylactic cyclosporine, azathioprine, and low-dose laronidase, while 1/3 patients in the second cohort met the antibody-titer criterion. The paper also reviews mechanistic and clinical evidence from Pompe disease showing that suppressing antibodies against alglucosidase alfa can improve enzyme-replacement efficacy, but the cited findings are not original data from this trial.

papers.title: Immune Modulation for Enzyme Replacement Therapy in A Female Patient With Hunter Syndrome.
papers.summary: In a single 3.5-year-old female patient with severe Hunter syndrome, concurrent rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin immune tolerance induction with idursulfase was associated with very low anti-idursulfase IgG titers, no clinically apparent adverse effects, and biochemical improvement. The paper also cites prior infantile Pompe disease experience showing that immune tolerance induction during the initiation of enzyme replacement therapy may prevent neutralizing anti-drug antibody development, supporting transfer to the analogous antibody-response mechanism in Pompe disease.

papers.title: Immune regulatory adjuvant approach to mitigate subcutaneous immunogenicity of monoclonal antibodies.
papers.summary: The paper shows in mice that co-formulating subcutaneous monoclonal antibodies with O-phospho-L-serine reduces anti-drug IgG responses, CD138+ plasma-cell differentiation, and prolonged CD4+ T-cell activation while preserving responses to an unrelated antigen. The authors also cite prior Pompe-mouse evidence that OPLS reduced anti-recombinant acid alpha glucosidase antibody titers and induced sustained hyporesponsiveness after GAA rechallenge.

papers.title: Anti-viral efficacy of a next-generation CD4-binding site bNAb in SHIV-infected animals in the absence of anti-drug antibody responses.
papers.summary: In chronically SHIV-infected rhesus macaques, pretreatment with an afucosylated rhesusized anti-CD20 antibody depleted peripheral B cells and prevented functionally significant anti-drug antibody responses during repeated VRC01v23 infusion. This supports B-cell depletion as a preclinical strategy for permitting repeated dosing and more accurate pharmacokinetic and antiviral assessment of human antibody therapeutics, although the small uncontrolled animal study does not establish clinical applicability.

papers.title: Methotrexate reduces antibody responses to recombinant human alpha-galactosidase A therapy in a mouse model of Fabry disease.
papers.summary: In alphaGAL knock-out mice with Fabry disease, short-course methotrexate combined with recombinant human alpha-galactosidase A significantly reduced enzyme-specific serum antibody and spleen-cell proliferative responses and suppressed development of enzyme-specific IgG. Methotrexate did not dampen robust ongoing antibody responses, and efficacy against long-term treatment-associated responses was incomplete.

papers.title: Anti-BlyS antibody reduces the immune reaction against enzyme and enhances the efficacy of enzyme replacement therapy in Fabry disease model mice.
papers.summary: In Fabry disease model mice, belimumab reduced B cells and anti-recombinant human alpha-galactosidase IgG titers after a single dose. Repeated maintenance dosing promoted immune tolerance in a dose-dependent manner, with high-dose treatment enhancing enzyme distribution and GL-3 clearance, although antibody formation was not completely prevented at the tested low dose.

unread.title: Case Report: Identification of Compound Heterozygous Mutations in a Patient With Late-Onset Glycogen Storage Disease Type II (Pompe Disease).
unread.why: The case provides concrete diagnostic evidence using GAA sequencing, muscle biopsy, and biochemical markers in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: A favorable outcome in an infantile-onset Pompe patient with cross reactive immunological material (CRIM) negative disease with high dose enzyme replacement therapy and adjusted immunomodulation.
unread.why: This case provides direct evidence for combining 40 mg/kg/week enzyme replacement therapy with staged immunomodulation in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Unusual Evolution of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Non-Compaction Myocardium in a Pompe Disease Patient.
unread.why: The report documents compassionate use of cipaglucosidase alfa plus miglustat and the resulting cardiac remodeling in infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: The phenotype, genotype, and outcome of infantile-onset Pompe disease in 18 Saudi patients.
unread.why: The 18-patient cohort reports ERT outcomes and suggests genotype-informed use of newborn screening and immunomodulation to improve infantile Pompe treatment.

unread.title: Molecular Diagnosis of Pompe Disease in the Genomic Era: Correlation with Acid Alpha-Glucosidase Activity in Dried Blood Spots.
unread.why: The study validates molecular panel testing combined with dried-blood-spot GAA activity, including reflex testing for pseudodeficiency and uncertain genotypes.

unread.title: Extensive digital health technology assessment detects subtle motor impairment in mild and asymptomatic Pompe disease.
unread.why: Digital gait and movement measurements detected subtle abnormalities in mild or asymptomatic Pompe disease despite normal conventional clinical scores.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation and CRIM status in Vietnamese children with Pompe disease: a single-center experience.
unread.why: The pediatric cohort demonstrates that GAA genotyping and CRIM status can predict disease course and inform treatment and screening strategies in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Consensus treatment recommendations for late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The consensus recommendations translate systematic evidence into a reusable treatment and monitoring strategy for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Infantile Pompe disease with intrauterine onset: a case report and literature review.
unread.why: The case demonstrates prompt acid alpha-glucosidase activity measurement and molecular testing to diagnose intrauterine-onset infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Detection of gene variants associated with recessive limb-girdle muscular weakness and Pompe disease in a global cohort of patients through the application of next-generation sequencing analysis.
unread.why: A validated 10-gene NGS approach diagnosed Pompe disease among 2,372 patients with limb-girdle muscular weakness and identified GAA variants.

unread.title: Sensory neuropathy in patients with Pompe disease: a case series in Iran.
unread.why: The study establishes neurophysiological and questionnaire-based methods for identifying previously unrecognized small- and large-fiber neuropathy in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Results of orthodontic procedure in a patient with classic infantile Pompe disease.
unread.why: Rapid maxillary expansion produced measurable improvement in speech and swallowing in a child with classic infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Integrating enzyme assay and molecular genetic testing for early diagnosis of infantile-onset Pompe disease: A case report.
unread.why: The case supports an integrated dried-blood-spot enzyme and molecular testing workflow for early diagnosis of infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: The impact of antibodies on clinical outcomes in diseases treated with therapeutic protein: lessons learned from infantile Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study identifies sustained antibody titers as a measurable predictor of poor enzyme-replacement outcomes and quantifies treatment response using several clinical endpoints.

unread.title: Early detection of Pompe disease by newborn screening is feasible: results from the Taiwan screening program.
unread.why: A large-scale pilot demonstrated the feasibility and earlier diagnostic yield of dried-blood-spot newborn screening for Pompe disease.

unread.title: Successful immune tolerance induction to enzyme replacement therapy in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease.
unread.why: Four CRIM-negative infants achieved sustained immune tolerance and clinical response to ERT using rituximab and methotrexate with or without IVIG.

unread.title: Neural deficits contribute to respiratory insufficiency in Pompe disease.
unread.why: The paper validates two Pompe animal models and provides direct evidence that neural respiratory dysfunction is a targetable component distinct from muscle weakness.

unread.title: Pompe disease in infants: improving the prognosis by newborn screening and early treatment.
unread.why: Newborn screening followed by prompt alglucosidase alfa treatment improved survival and developmental and cardiac outcomes in infants with Pompe disease.

unread.title: Pompe disease: design, methodology, and early findings from the Pompe Registry.
unread.why: The international registry provides a large reusable dataset and natural-history framework for studying heterogeneous Pompe disease progression and treatment outcomes.

unread.title: Observational clinical study in juvenile-adult glycogenosis type 2 patients undergoing enzyme replacement therapy for up to 4 years.
unread.why: This multicenter study reports long-term alglucosidase alfa treatment and clinically measurable outcomes in juvenile and adult Pompe disease.

unread.title: The pharmacological chaperone 1-deoxynojirimycin increases the activity and lysosomal trafficking of multiple mutant forms of acid alpha-glucosidase.
unread.why: The study shows that 1-deoxynojirimycin increases activity, maturation, and lysosomal trafficking of multiple mutant GAA forms, supporting its therapeutic evaluation.

unread.title: A chaperone enhances blood α-glucosidase activity in Pompe disease patients treated with enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: Patient data show that N-butyldeoxynojirimycin increases circulating alpha-glucosidase activity when combined with ERT, indicating improved recombinant enzyme stability.

unread.title: LOPED study: looking for an early diagnosis in a late-onset Pompe disease high-risk population.
unread.why: The LOPED study validates dried-blood-spot screening and confirmatory testing for late-onset Pompe disease in a high-risk population.

unread.title: Response of 33 UK patients with infantile-onset Pompe disease to enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: The cohort documents ERT response and clinically relevant prognostic outcomes in infantile-onset Pompe disease, including the impact of CRIM status and immunomodulation.

unread.title: Molecular and functional characterization of eight novel GAA mutations in Italian infants with Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study provides experimental and computational methods for characterizing eight GAA mutations and predicting their functional consequences in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Screening for later-onset Pompe's disease in patients with paucisymptomatic hyperCKemia.
unread.why: This screening study demonstrates a diagnostic pathway for finding preclinical later-onset Pompe disease in patients with unexplained hyperCKemia.

unread.title: Molecular diagnosis of German patients with late-onset glycogen storage disease type II.
unread.why: The study establishes a rapid genetic-testing strategy that identifies 94% of late-onset Pompe cases and supports quick diagnosis before enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Sensitivity of whole exome sequencing in detecting infantile- and late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The diagnostic accuracy study quantifies when whole-exome sequencing succeeds or fails in Pompe disease and identifies safeguards and fallback testing strategies.

unread.title: Clinical characteristics and genotypes in the ADVANCE baseline data set, a comprehensive cohort of US children and adolescents with Pompe disease.
unread.why: The ADVANCE dataset supplies standardized clinical, functional, cardiac, and genotype resources for a large treated pediatric Pompe cohort.

unread.title: Splice modulating antisense oligonucleotides restore some acid-alpha-glucosidase activity in cells derived from patients with late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study experimentally identifies an antisense oligonucleotide that restores GAA transcript, protein, and enzyme activity in late-onset Pompe patient cells.

unread.title: Six-Minute Walk Distance Is a Useful Outcome Measure to Detect Motor Decline in Treated Late-Onset Pompe Disease Patients.
unread.why: A two-year comparative study identifies six-minute walk distance as a sensitive endpoint for detecting motor decline in treated late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: A rapid and non-invasive proteomic analysis using DBS and buccal swab for multiplexed second-tier screening of Pompe disease and Mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: Reports a validated rapid second-tier screening assay that directly quantifies endogenous GAA in DBS and buccal swabs and distinguishes Pompe patients from carriers and pseudodeficient samples.

unread.title: Advances in Pompe Disease Treatment: From Enzyme Replacement to Gene Therapy.
unread.why: Summarizes approved, clinical-stage, and preclinical Pompe treatments, including ERT and AAV gene therapy supported by phase I/II trial data.

unread.title: Late-onset Pompe disease associated with polyneuropathy.
unread.why: Provides patient evidence that peripheral neuropathy can affect late-onset Pompe disease and supports proprioceptive physiotherapy and ongoing disability-oriented care.

unread.title: Long-Term Outcome of Infantile Onset Pompe Disease Patients Treated with Enzyme Replacement Therapy - Data from a German-Austrian Cohort.
unread.why: Reports long-term clinical outcomes in 15 infantile-onset Pompe patients treated with alglucosidase alfa and provides outcome measures for evaluating newer treatment strategies.

unread.title: Swallow Prognosis and Follow-Up Protocol in Infantile Onset Pompe Disease.
unread.why: Develops and tests a follow-up protocol using FOIS and videofluoroscopy to predict feeding outcomes and guide monitoring and gastrostomy decisions in infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Experience with the Urinary Tetrasaccharide Metabolite for Pompe Disease in the Diagnostic Laboratory.
unread.why: Reports a confirmatory urinary tetrasaccharide assay and reference intervals for Pompe disease while also demonstrating limitations for treatment-response monitoring.

unread.title: Clinical course, mutations and its functional characteristics of infantile-onset Pompe disease in Thailand.
unread.why: Uses cell-based GAA expression, enzyme activity, immunoblotting, and structural analysis to classify novel GAA variants and provide a proposed substitute for CRIM assessment.

unread.title: Development of a clinically validated in vitro functional assay to assess pathogenicity of novel GAA variants in patients with Pompe disease identified via newborn screening.
unread.why: Reports a clinically validated in vitro functional system that reproducibly distinguishes pathogenic, benign, and pseudodeficiency GAA variants and helps classify variants of uncertain significance.

unread.title: Pompe disease ascertained through The Lantern Project, 2018-2021: Next-generation sequencing and enzymatic testing to overcome obstacles to diagnosis.
unread.why: Reports 140 confirmed Pompe cases diagnosed through a reusable diagnostic program combining enzymology, biomarkers, sequencing, and a focused neuromuscular panel.

unread.title: Development of high sustained anti-drug antibody titers and corresponding clinical decline in a late-onset Pompe disease patient after 11+ years on enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: Shows that surveillance for high anti-drug antibody titers and urinary Glc4 can identify immune-mediated ERT failure and that immunomodulation improves biomarker and clinical outcomes.

unread.title: High-risk screening of late-onset Pompe disease: A different early portrait in China.
unread.why: Prospectively validates a DBS GAA MS/MS plus sequencing strategy for identifying late-onset Pompe disease in high-risk patients and distinguishes true deficiency from pseudodeficiency.

unread.title: Investigating Late-Onset Pompe Prevalence in Neuromuscular Medicine Academic Practices: The IPaNeMA Study.
unread.why: This study validates a two-stage GAA enzyme and molecular screening workflow and creates a multicenter late-onset Pompe disease cohort and registry.

unread.title: Improved Enzyme Replacement Therapy with Cipaglucosidase Alfa/Miglustat in Infantile Pompe Disease.
unread.why: The report provides patient-level evidence that switching from alglucosidase alfa to cipaglucosidase alfa/miglustat improved respiratory, cardiac, and motor outcomes in infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Immunophenotype associated with high sustained antibody titers against enzyme replacement therapy in infantile-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study identifies an immune biomarker signature that distinguishes patients with high sustained anti-ERT antibody titers and could guide immunomodulatory development.

unread.title: A generic assay for the identification of splicing variants that induce nonsense-mediated decay in Pompe disease.
unread.why: The paper both extends a functional GAA splicing assay to detect nonsense-mediated-decay events and experimentally demonstrates an ASO that restores canonical splicing and GAA activity.

unread.title: Correlation of GAA Genotype and Acid-α-Glucosidase Enzyme Activity in Hungarian Patients with Pompe Disease.
unread.why: The study applies combined enzymatic and genetic testing to Pompe patients and identifies genotype-specific GAA activity patterns useful for diagnosis and prognosis.

unread.title: Bioimpedance Phase Angle as a Prognostic Tool in Late-Onset Pompe Disease: A Single-Centre Prospective Study With a 15-year Follow-Up.
unread.why: Prospective 15-year data indicate that low phase angle can serve as a low-cost prognostic marker of long-term ERT response in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: L-alanine supplementation in Pompe disease (IOPD): a potential therapeutic implementation for patients on ERT? A case report.
unread.why: This first case report shows that L-alanine added to ERT was associated with increased fat mass and reduced resting energy expenditure in a child with infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Optimizing clinical outcomes: The journey of twins with CRIM-negative infantile-onset Pompe disease on high-dose enzyme replacement therapy and immunomodulation.
unread.why: The twins' clinical data support early high-dose ERT combined with immune tolerance induction and a subsequent switch to avalglucosidase alfa in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Function, structure and quality of striated muscles in the lower extremities in patients with late onset Pompe Disease-an MRI study.
unread.why: The study provides patient data showing that quantitative Dixon MRI can characterize lower-extremity muscle quality and potentially monitor longitudinal changes during ERT.

unread.title: Assessment of Dysphonia in Children with Pompe Disease Using Auditory-Perceptual and Acoustic/Physiologic Methods.
unread.why: The study validates perceptual and objective acoustic or physiologic measurements for quantifying dysphonia and respiratory-laryngeal dysfunction in children with Pompe disease.

unread.title: Base editing rescues acid α-glucosidase function in infantile-onset Pompe disease patient-derived cells.
unread.why: Base editing directly corrects three pathogenic GAA nonsense variants in patient-derived cells, restoring enzyme activity and reducing lysosomal burden.

unread.title: Infantile-onset Pompe disease complicated by sickle cell anemia: Case report and management considerations.
unread.why: This case reports treated infantile-onset Pompe disease with alglucosidase alfa, immune tolerance induction, and management of a concurrent genetic disease.

unread.title: Effectiveness of Respiratory Muscle Training in Pompe Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
unread.why: The systematic review and meta-analysis provides pooled evidence that respiratory muscle training improves respiratory strength in Pompe disease, with quantified clinical outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical, pathological and genetic features as well as follow-up of 68 patients with late-onset Pompe disease: a single-center retrospective study.
unread.why: The study provides Pompe-specific real-world evidence on ERT survival and functional outcomes, earlier treatment timing, and candidate pathological and clinical measures.

unread.title: Pompe disease: a neuromuscular disease with respiratory muscle involvement.
unread.why: The review summarizes clinical-trial evidence for recombinant GAA therapy and practical approaches to respiratory management and early diagnosis in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Multisystem late onset Pompe disease (LOPD): an update on clinical aspects.
unread.why: This disease-specific review describes established ERT and diagnostic strategies while identifying additional clinical targets and emerging treatments for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Infantile Pompe disease on ERT: update on clinical presentation, musculoskeletal management, and exercise considerations.
unread.why: The paper reviews beneficial ERT outcomes and provides existing exercise and musculoskeletal management strategies for patients with residual weakness.

unread.title: Immunological challenges and approaches to immunomodulation in Pompe disease: a literature review.
unread.why: The review compiles tested immunomodulation strategies and antibody biomarkers used to improve safety and efficacy of ERT in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Autophagy in skeletal muscle: implications for Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study supplies a Pompe-specific animal model and evidence that failed muscle autophagy is measurable and can interfere with ERT delivery.

unread.title: Diagnosis of Pompe disease: muscle biopsy vs blood-based assays.
unread.why: The paper directly compares diagnostic approaches and identifies blood-based GAA activity measurement as an effective first-line test for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Physical therapy management of Pompe disease.
unread.why: The review describes physical therapy strategies and motor and respiratory assessments applicable to patients receiving Pompe disease ERT.

unread.title: Newborn screening for Pompe disease: synthesis of the evidence and development of screening recommendations.
unread.why: The systematic review reports screening performance and recommendations, including the trade-off between sensitivity and false positives, for early detection of infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Clinical guidelines for late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The guideline provides an actionable diagnostic pathway, follow-up approach, and early ERT recommendations for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Avalglucosidase alfa: First Approval.
unread.why: This review reports the development and regulatory approval of avalglucosidase alfa specifically for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Current avenues of gene therapy in Pompe disease.
unread.why: The review summarizes Pompe-specific gene-therapy platforms, clinical-trial evidence, and methods for vector delivery, immune management, and expression optimization.

unread.title: Recommendations for Infantile-Onset and Late-Onset Pompe Disease: An Iranian Consensus.
unread.why: This disease-specific consensus provides operational algorithms for diagnosis, treatment selection, and longitudinal management of infantile- and late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Establishing Pompe Disease Newborn Screening: The Role of Industry.
unread.why: The paper describes two validated dried-blood-spot GAA screening assays and their implementation through pilot and national newborn-screening programs.

unread.title: Therapeutic thoroughfares for adults living with Pompe disease.
unread.why: The review summarizes clinical and long-term evidence for multiple existing and investigational therapeutic approaches in adult Pompe disease.

unread.title: [Pompe disease treated with enzyme replacement therapy in pregnancy].
unread.why: This case-based report provides direct evidence on the tolerability and use of enzyme replacement therapy in pregnant Pompe disease.

unread.title: Quantitative super-resolution imaging with deep learning segmentation reveals early mitochondrial network remodeling and altered mitochondria-lysosome interactions in Pompe disease muscle
unread.why: The study develops and validates an imaging and deep-learning framework that quantifies disease-stage mitochondrial remodeling and organelle interactions in Pompe muscle.

unread.title: Intracellular Membrane Repair Dysregulation and Accumulation of Mature Myostatin Protein are Novel Markers of Muscle Pathophysiology in Pompe Disease
unread.why: The study experimentally identifies membrane-repair proteins and mature myostatin as tissue and serum-relevant markers associated with Pompe muscle pathology.

unread.title: GC801-enabled AAV gene therapy in a neonate with Pompe disease
unread.why: The report shows that a single GC801 dose safely reduced pre-existing anti-AAV9 antibodies and enabled successful GC301 gene delivery and increased GAA activity in an infant with Pompe disease.

unread.title: Live-cell Raman imaging of Pompe disease reveals extensive sarcoplasmic accumulations of precipitated glycogen
unread.why: The study develops and applies a Raman imaging assay that detects disease-associated glycogen localization and precipitation in Pompe patient muscle cells and can assess glycogen-targeted therapies.

unread.title: A Genome Engineered Human Embryonic Stem Cell line to Investigate Pompe Disease
unread.why: The authors generate a scalable, genome-edited hESC model with GAA deficiency, lysosomal accumulation, and muscle-cell phenotypes suitable for therapeutic screening.

unread.title: Clinical and therapeutic impact of whole-exome sequencing in inherited neuromuscular disorders: first autonomous cohort from Algeria
unread.why: The cohort demonstrates an autonomous WES workflow that resolved a genetically masked case of infantile-onset Pompe disease and enabled timely enzyme replacement therapy and related management.

unread.title: Umbilical Cord Blood Sampling for Newborn Screening of Pompe Disease and the Detection of a Novel Pathogenic Variant and Pseudodeficiency Variants in an Asian population
unread.why: The study validates umbilical cord blood as a newborn-screening sample and establishes an assay workflow for detecting GAA deficiency and distinguishing pseudodeficiency variants.

unread.title: Assessing Gene Therapy Efficacy in Infantile-Onset Pompe Disease: Myocardial Native T1 Values of CMR.
unread.why: The report identifies serial native T1 and myocardial lesion measurements as outcome measures that changed after gene therapy in infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Reduction of false-positive results with biochemical second-tier testing for newborn screening of Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study evaluates a second-tier biochemical and postanalytic strategy that substantially reduces false positives while detecting confirmed infantile-onset cases.
